findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P1] pilotFreezeCheck freezes N at the Wilson LOWER bound, which is NOT conservative under the pooled two-proportion formula: n peaks where pbar=(p1+(p1-mde))/2 is nearest 0.5, so a lower bound below ~0.5+mde/2 yields a SMALLER n than the observed baseline (counterexample: pilot 36/60, CI width 0.2406 freezes, lower 0.47366 -> 56/arm vs observed 0.60 -> 62/arm). The plan S7 wording (freeze at lower bound, conservative) shares the flaw. Fix the tool: freeze at the N-MAXIMIZING baseline within the Wilson CI (analytic max at p*=0.5+mde/2 clamped to the CI), document the deviation from the S7 letter as satisfying its conservative INTENT; flag plan S7 for a docs follow-up.

[host-2 Codex P1] buildLedger binds only the protocolHash, not the frozen task-class MEMBERSHIP: validateManifest accepts trapClass not-in-protocol with trapGroup in_store, so unregistered fixtures can enter the run under a valid protocol hash. Fix: consume doc.taskClasses from guardFrozenProtocol and reject rows whose trapClass is not a member of the frozen group matching its trapGroup; add selfcheck case.

[host-2 Codex P2] The adequacy report includes only unpaired reference sizing; M5 requires unpaired reference + McNemar paired sizing. Fix: add a paired section (McNemar nPairs at the live point and the seeded band max, discordant cells derived under the documented independence approximation p01=p1(1-p2), p10=p2(1-p1), with optional explicit override in config) to adequacy-report.json and .md; add selfcheck case.

[host-2 Codex P2] Protocol validation rejects only inStore/heldOut overlap; a class can be in clean AND a fault group although clean tasks must never pool into the fault baseline. Fix: reject pairwise overlap across all three groups; add selfcheck case.

[host-2 Codex P2] Seals are self-authenticating (tamper+rehash passes) and validateFrozenProtocol ignores the sidecar protocolHash field it stores. Partial fix in-scope: verify sidecar.protocolHash === doc.protocolHash; document the threat model (tamper-EVIDENCE for accidental drift; external anchoring of the protocolHash into story/run evidence is the M6 runner responsibility). Full external anchoring is out of S1 scope by design.

[host-2 Codex P3] guardImmutable has a TOCTOU window between the guard and the three renames. Fix: re-check the guard immediately before the writes (narrows the window; single-host tooling tier documented).
[host-2 Codex P3] protocol-selfcheck leaks the two extra mkdtemp roots (ablation-p1/p2) and snapDir (never removed in finally). Fix: track and remove all temp roots.

[host-2 Codex P3] protocol.mjs usage line is inaccurate per subcommand (hash needs only --config; validate needs no --config; freeze takes experimentId from the config). Fix: per-subcommand usage output.

sample-size.mjs main() has no try/catch wrapper: JSON.parse failures (malformed config file) and readFileSync errors (file not found) surface as raw Node.js stack traces rather than the clean 'ERROR: <message>' pattern used consistently by protocol.mjs and pair-ledger.mjs. The quality review scope explicitly requires 'JSON parse failures produce useful errors'. Demonstration: node sample-size.mjs report --config=/nonexistent.json exits 1 but emits a 10-line stack trace from node:fs:442 instead of a clean ERROR line. Fix: wrap main() body in try { ... } catch (err) { console.error('ERROR: ' + err.message); process.exit(1); }

sample-size.mjs uses plain writeFileSync (not atomic temp-then-rename) for both adequacy-report.json and adequacy-report.md writes (lines 262-263). protocol.mjs and pair-ledger.mjs both define and use a writeAtomic(path, text) helper that writes to a .tmp-<pid> path then renames. A crash or SIGKILL between the two writeFileSync calls leaves a valid .json alongside a truncated or absent .md, and a crash mid-write leaves a half-written .json. The quality review scope requires atomic writes for every artifact write. Fix: add writeAtomic helper matching protocol.mjs pattern and use it for both output files.
